root_idea.summary: The root expresses causing something to go away, especially by removing its trace or effect.
root_idea.development: The basic orientation develops from making clouds or other things pass away to erasing writing, traces, signs, or effects. The noun مَحْوَةٌ for the north wind is explained through its dispersing of clouds.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form مَحَا rather than the internal inflected QAC lemma.

senses.definition: To efface, erase, obliterate, or cancel something, causing it or its trace or effect to disappear.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I verb of removal and disappearance. In the Quran it is used for divine erasure, including erasing what is willed and erasing a sign; the same general removal sense covers making something pass away or cancelling its effect.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Core effacing, erasing, cancelling, and removing a trace are directly represented.
Dispersing clouds is an atmospheric example of making something pass away, not an independent lexical branch.
Dispelling night is covered by the general removal and disappearance sense.
Removing diseases and sins is an application of cancellation or removal of an effect.
Effacing evil conduct is an application of the same cancellation and effacement sense.
